mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately eroding profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of high unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in INDPRO above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% for three consecutive months indicates strengthening industrial production, which typically coincides with improved corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising industrial production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL by more than 0.5% over two months signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with falling inflation, which typically supports equity valuations through stable real rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL falls > -0.5% over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of both rising rates and falling inflation (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their 6-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals weakening housing and overall demand, which tends to drag on consumer discretionary earnings and depress equity prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 6-month MA and HOUST < 6-month MA for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of both falling GDP and housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average by more than 1% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong payroll growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between rising RSAFS and subsequent S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as increased household savings can signal anticipated future consumption and corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS increases and positive 5-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant at the 5% level in out-of-sample tests.
